Sub:   Notice of the Annual General Meeting along with Integrated Annual 
Report of the Company for the financial year 202 5-26 
 
Dear Sir,  
 This is to inform you that t he Thirtie th Annual General Meeting ( “AGM” ) of the 
Company will be held on Thursday , June 25, 2026  at 2. 30 p.m. IST through 
Video Conference / Other Audio Visual Means  in accordance with the applicable 
circulars issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and the Securities and 
Exchange Board of India.   
 
Pursuant to Regulation 34(1) of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015  (“SEBI Listing 
Regulations” ), we are submitting herewith the Integrated Annual Report of the 
Company along with  the Notice of AGM and Business Responsibility and 
Sustainability Report for the financial year 202 5-26, which is being sent through 
electronic mode to the Members . 
 As per Regulation 36(1)(b) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, the letter mentioning 
web-link including the exact path, where complete details of the Annual Report 
are available,  is being sent to those member(s) who have not registered their 
email address(es) either with the Company or with any Depository or Registrar 
and Share Transfer Agent (RTA) of the Company.  
 We would like to further inform that the Company has fixed Thursday , June 18, 
2026  as the cut -off date  for ascertaining the names of the members holding 
shares either in physical form or in dematerialised form, who will be entitled to 
cast their votes electronically in respect of the businesses to be transacted as per the Notice of the AGM and to attend th e AGM.  
 The Integrated Annual Report containing the Notice is also uploaded on the 
Company’s website  and can be accessed at  www.adanipower.com .

Integrated Reporting
This is Adani Power Limited’s (Adani Power or APL or Company) third Integrated Annual Report <IR>, showcasing 
performance for FY 2025-26, offering a comprehensive overview of its financial, non-financial and operational performance, strategic advancements, and progress toward long-term value creation for our stakeholders. It outlines the Company’s strategic positioning, future outlook, and key priorities, while reflecting a strong commitment to transparency and enabling stakeholders to gain a holistic understanding of its business model and value delivery approach.

Reporting Scope, Boundary 
and Period
This report encompasses Adani 
Power Limited’s corporate functions, APL assets and its subsidiaries- thermal power plants and solar power plant. The scope reflects the Company’s operational and financial boundary, unless stated otherwise. The reporting period extends from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026.
Approach to Materiality
The <IR> focuses on matters that influence our ability to create value across the short, medium and long term. Material topics are identified through internal assessments of our strategy, business model, stakeholder expectations and the external environment. Issues identified through our  FY 2023-24 materiality assessment are already integrated into long-term planning and are reviewed annually to refine strategic focus and ESG priorities.
Financial capital: Our funding 
strength and capital management discipline that minimises project risks and financing costs, supporting growth and stakeholder value creation
Human capital: Our people’s skills, capabilities and development initiatives that drive performance and industry readinessManufactured capital: Our power assets and technology investments that enhance productivity, efficiency and operational consistency
Natural capital: Our environmental stewardship focuses on minimising impact, conserving resources and meeting regulatory expectationsSocial & Relationship capital: Our stakeholder relationships, including customers, vendors and communities, that enable business continuity and social impactIntellectual capital: Our knowledge and experience in power generation sector that strengthen competitiveness and support market leadership

Pedigree 
The Adani portfolio of 
companies is headquartered in Ahmedabad, India. It was founded and promoted in 1988 by Mr Gautam Adani, whose foresight has shaped some of the most critical pillars of India's modern infrastructure. What began as a trading enterprise is now one of India’s most dynamic, diversified, and forward-looking conglomerates comprising 13 listed companies.Vision
To be a world-class leader in businesses that enrich lives and contribute to nations in building infrastructure through sustainable value creation.Culture

A Legacy of  
Vision, Leadership and Nationhood 
The Adani portfolio of 
companies is India’s largest integrated infrastructure platform, synonymous with national progress, scale, and purpose. Over the years, it has consistently delivered best-in-class growth with robust cash flows and financial discipline. The portfolio is today among India’s largest contributors to national revenues and taxes, and most trusted corporate groups, redefining economic development. Guided by a nation-first 
ethos, the Adani portfolio of companies is investing at scale in critical infrastructure and new-age sectors to enable ‘Viksit Bharat’. It is equally committed to sustainable development and creating value for all stakeholders, with the philosophy of ‘Growth with Goodness’ at its core. 
At the Adani portfolio of 
companies, every action, every idea pursued and every forward leap is driven by the goal of making India rise stronger, stand self-reliant, and thrive sustainably.

Thermal generation continues 
to provide the stability required to balance renewable variability and ensure consistent supply, while states sharpen their focus on long-term procurement to secure reliable, dispatchable capacity. This rising demand calls for capacity that is scalable and dependable.
Our scale is expanding, 
aligned with long-term demand

strong operational base of  18,150 MW, with the acquisition and rapid revival of the 600 MW  Butibori plant. Our growth trajectory remains well defined, supported by a locked-in pipeline of 23,720 MW and clear demand visibility.
This expansion reflects our 
approach to capacity creation, aligned with long-term supply arrangements. As scale expands, the need for 
consistent and timely execution becomes more critical..
Execution continues to gain speed, 
anchored in discipline and consistency. Progress across the expansion pipeline remains aligned to defined milestones, supported by a structured framework and brownfield development. Supply chain readiness stays firm, with critical equipment secured in advance. We have secured 100% of BTG requirements for the pipeline, strengthening visibility and keeping execution on track.
This momentum draws strength from 
a stable, well-balanced model. A large share of capacity remains tied to long- and medium-term contracts, ensuring revenue visibility and priority dispatch, while a measured portion stays open to benefit from merchant markets. Availability-linked tariffs support steady cost recovery, backed by high uptime and efficient operations. Presence across key industrial regions, combined with competitive costs and flexible fuel strategies, keeps the system responsive as it continues to scale. 
..whereas, intelligence, moving 
alongside infrastructure, is enabling sustained performance

Real-time monitoring through centralised control systems allows continuous visibility across assets, while analytics-led interventions guide operations closer to optimal thresholds. From combustion optimisation to load management, intelligence is increasingly embedded within core processes, improving efficiency while reducing variability in performance.
Predictive capabilities continue to 
strengthen reliability. Machine learning models identify early signals across equipment, enabling timely intervention and preventing disruptions. Automation reduces manual dependencies, while digital platforms build workforce readiness to operate in a data-driven environment. As infrastructure expands, these systems ensure that performance scales with it, allowing assets to respond, adapt, and deliver with consistency.

Dear Stakeholders,
India’s economic growth aspirations are tied 
irrevocably to the availability of reliable, affordable, and scalable power supply. The geopolitical upheavals witnessed in our neighbourhood emphasize the critical need for enhancing energy security and localising fuel supplies with a vision to achieve energy sovereignty.  At the same time, India’s environmental and sustainability goals foretell a need for responsive and dependable power supply across regions and demand cycles to support an increasingly complex energy mix. In this context, reliability and flexibility are being reimagined. They are being shaped by power infrastructure that advances with speed and agility, and by systems that enhance predictability, sharpen control, strengthen operating discipline, and improve performance continuously.
‘Accelerating Infrastructure. 
Leveraging Intelligence.’ reflects the path we are pursuing. Our growth is aligned with India’s rising need for baseload power and accelerating peak demand, and supported by a secured expansion pipeline, long-term offtake visibility and digitally enabled operations that help convert scale into consistent outcomes
Where we operate
India’s electricity sector is entering a sustained growth phase, supported by industrialisation, urban expansion and rising energy intensity across sectors. The momentum is being shaped by structural demand from emerging segments such as electric mobility, data centres and manufacturing-led growth.
The rise in demand is also strengthening the 
need for reliable base-load supply to maintain grid stability. Renewable energy continues to scale rapidly, yet its variable nature makes dependable thermal generation critical for balancing supply and supporting uninterrupted power availability. The evolving landscape emphasises a shifting towards consistent, responsive and reliable power supply, supported by systems that can manage complexity and sustain performance across cycles.We are built for this phase
Our positioning is anchored in structural strengths that align closely with India’s evolving energy requirements. As the largest private thermal power producer in the country, with a portfolio of 18,150 MW across multiple states, we operate with the flexibility to serve diverse demand centres and benefit from economies of scale. Our ability to acquire and turn around stressed power assets, amply demonstrated by converting more than 7GW of capacity into profitable and cash-generating assets, reflects our pragmatic approach to attain rapid growth, consolidate key resources, and create enduring value. 
Operational performance continues to be 
a key differentiator. We have maintained plant availability above 90% over several years, supported by a strong digital focus. This consistency, combined with industry-leading EBITDA margins of around 38% in the thermal segment, reflects our ability to convert scale into sustained performance. Our rich experience and capabilities in coal sourcing and end-to-end logistics management provide us with greater control over input costs and supply reliability.
Our expansion is supported by high execution 
readiness, with land availability secured and equipment ordering completed for the entire growth pipeline. A higher share of brownfield projects enables faster commissioning and better capital efficiency. Long-term PPAs, backed by domestic fuel linkages and availability-based tariffs, provide visibility of revenues and stability of returns, reinforcing our position in a market where reliability is becoming increasingly critical.
Advancing our operational discipline
Our growth is anchored in one of the most significant capacity expansion programmes undertaken in the sector. We are progressing towards a targeted capacity of 41,870 MW by FY 2031-32, with plans to add approximately 23,720 MW on a medium-term basis. This scale of addition is materially higher than what has been achieved historically, with our existing portfolio of 18,150 MW built over nearly two decades. Our capital expenditure programme, estimated at

Based on current performance levels, we expect to generate aggregate adequate fund flows from operations over the next six years that would allow us to fund the majority portion of this expansion through internal accruals. This reduces dependence on external financing, removes financial closure risks and provides greater flexibility in capital deployment.
Execution readiness remains a key focus. 
We have secured land availability and completed ordering of critical equipment, including boiler, turbine and generator packages, for the entire expansion pipeline. A significant share of the expansion is being undertaken through brownfield development, allowing us to leverage existing infrastructure, optimise timelines and improve capital efficiency.
The power of embedded intelligence
As we scale, maintaining consistency across operations becomes increasingly critical. Our focus is on embedding intelligence within systems and processes to strengthen control, improve efficiency and sustain performance across our portfolio. This approach enables us to manage growing complexity while ensuring stability in operations.
We are leveraging the establishment of a 
centralised Energy Network Operation Center (ENOC) in Ahmedabad, which provides real-time monitoring and diagnosis of assets across multiple states. This platform enables optimised power scheduling and supports faster, data-led decision-making. Our use of AI/ML-driven analytics supports early-stage anomaly detection and predictive maintenance, improving mean time between failures and reducing unplanned outages. These capabilities are further supported by our Analytical Center of Excellence, which strengthens analytics adoption across operations, and by supply chain intelligence tools such as our fuel tracker, which enables real-time monitoring and optimisation of coal sourcing and logistics.The convergence of physical infrastructure with intelligent systems is enhancing asset productivity, improving reliability and optimising costs across operations. It is also enabling more responsive planning and coordination, particularly in areas such as fuel sourcing and logistics. As capacity expands, this integrated approach allows us to accelerate execution timelines while maintaining consistency, ensuring that growth is supported by operational discipline and sustained performance.
Sustaining our performance
Our financial position reflects the strength of our operating model and the discipline underlying our growth strategy. We delivered a Continuing EBITDA of ` 21,285 crore in FY 2025-26, with reported EBITDA for the year ending March 2026 at ` 23,431 crore. This sustained performance is supported by high plant availability, efficient cost structures and stable offtake through long-term PPAs.
Our credit profile has strengthened significantly, 
with ratings of AA/Stable from CRISIL, ICRA, India Ratings and CARE, an eight-notch upgrade since 2020. This progression reflects improved earnings visibility and a resilient balance sheet, enhancing our ability to access capital on competitive terms and support long-term growth.
We maintain a healthy capital structure, 
with a net debt to continuing EBITDA ratio of 2.12x during the period. This provides adequate headroom to fund our expansion programme while preserving financial flexibility. project-linked community development initiatives embedded within new capacity additions, our engagement with communities is becoming more extensive and structured. As more projects move into execution, this integrated approach ensures that development around our operations progresses alongside business growth.
Governance and social priorities remain integral 
to our approach. We continue to strengthen diversity and inclusion, with a targeted increase in female representation and focused initiatives such as ‘Unnati’ to build leadership capabilities. Our commitment to a safe and respectful workplace is reflected in a zero-tolerance approach to POSH, with no reported cases during the year. As our operations expand, our social investments are also scaling, with CSR commitments approaching ` 280 crore annually and additional project-linked community initiatives embedded within new developments. This ensures our growth and meaningful contribution to the community at large.
Looking ahead with confidence

Operating responsibly
Our approach to sustainability is integrated at the core of our operations. We focus on improving efficiency, strengthening governance and building long-term resilience. As we expand towards our targeted capacity, we continue to embed resource discipline and operational accountability across our portfolio.
Our environmental efforts are guided by a 
structured pathway focused on efficiency and emissions reduction. The use of supercritical and ultra-supercritical technologies enables higher thermal efficiency, while initiatives such as biomass co-firing support a reduction in coal intensity. We have maintained 100% ash utilisation, achieved zero liquid discharge across all hinterland plants and continue to manage water intensity below regulatory thresholds. These measures improve resource efficiency while strengthening operational sustainability.
Climate considerations are being embedded into 
decision-making through Climate Change Risk Assessments across locations and the adoption of an internal carbon pricing framework. Our long-term roadmap towards Net Zero by 2070 is supported by a phased approach, combining near-term efficiency improvements with future technology adoption.

About the Company
Built for Power 
Leadership
We are India’s largest 
thermal power producer and a leading baseload generation company. We play an important role in meeting India’s rising power needs, supplying reliable and affordable power to households, businesses and industries, and supporting the country’s economic progress. Our business model 
combines long-term PPAs with selectively positioned open capacity, enabling healthy returns and stable value creation. Strong capital and liquidity management, along with disciplined risk controls, have strengthened the balance sheet and contributed to multiple credit rating upgrades since 2018.
Inbuilt, irreplicable structural advantages drive us as the best power generation play in India. These advantages have been built over decades and reflect our deep operating experience. In-house coal sourcing, end-to-end logistics management and strong fuel security bring consistency to plant operations. Efficient operations and maintenance practices, supported by technology, help us achieve higher availability and competitive costs across sites.
Our Profile 
Adani Power, headquartered in Ahmedabad, started operations in 2006 with the commencement of construction of its first power plant in Mundra, Gujarat. Over the years, we have established a large diversified portfolio, comprising 18,150 MW modern and efficient power generating assets that cater to eight states in India, comprising Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Haryana, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, 
Our Vision 
Be a transformative force in power generation, empowering lives and contributing to the energy security of nations by providing sustainable, affordable and reliable power.As part of our sustainability drive,  we keep on improving on emission and water intensity, circular economy driven waste management practices, occupational health & safety. Engagements Advanced  
with Intelligence Stakeholder Engagement 
Meaningful engagement with stakeholders supports informed decision-
making. We follow a structured approach to identify and address stakeholder expectations, enabling actions that align organisational priorities with stakeholder interests. This approach contributes to sustained value creation and supports the delivery of our long-term commitments. 
Our Stakeholder Engagement Mechanism 
The Board-level Stakeholder 
Relationship Committee focusses on key stakeholder groups such as investors, analysts, and shareholders. We set clear targets, review performance regularly, and disclose progress to reinforce accountability and strengthen stakeholder trust.Stakeholder engagement is guided by a defined Stakeholder Engagement Policy, which ensures transparency and consistency across the process. Oversight is provided by the Corporate Responsibility Committee, which reports engagement outcomes to the Board of Directors. Identifying and Engaging with Material Stakeholders
We follow a three-pronged approach to incorporate stakeholder inputs, address concerns, and drive continuous improvement.
Identification
Determine stakeholder groups that directly or indirectly influence, or are influenced, by our business activitiesAnalyse and 
Prioritisation
Assess and rank stakeholders 
based on mutual dependence, responsibility, and influence on our businessEngagement and  
Collaboration 
Implement a structured 
engagement plan tailored to each stakeholder group to build constructive relationships and support sustainable, mutually beneficial outcomes

Intelligence Strengthening 
our Material FocusMaterial Matters 
Managing material matters supports long-term value creation and strategic 
clarity. The assessment process evaluates factors influencing business performance, stakeholder expectations, and future resilience. Insights from material priorities shape resource planning, operational focus, and enterprise-wide risk and opportunity management through our Integrated Management Systems (IMS).
Our Approach to Materiality Assessment
customers, communities, academia, 
regulators, and media informed topic relevance and future significance.
The review strengthened the prominence 
of themes such as digitalisation, data privacy and information security, employee development and retention, labour practices, diversity, equity and inclusion, supply chain responsibility, and lifecycle management of assets.A double materiality assessment was completed in FY 2023-24 and reviewed in FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26 to maintain alignment with the evolving sustainability environment. The assessment followed GRI 3: Material Topics 2021 and European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) General Disclosures, recognising impact and financial materiality as key dimensions. Stakeholder engagement across investors, employees, suppliers, Identifying and Prioritising 
Matters of Importance
The boundary of the double 
materiality assessment is same as the reporting boundary and applies across the corporate office, thermal and solar operations, and subsidiaries. 
Impact materiality classification 
relied on our operating context, sector exposure, and business relationships to establish actual and potential implications on the economy, environment, and people. Impacts were evaluated by nature, duration, reversibility, scale, and likelihood, enabling severity-based prioritisation.
Financial materiality evaluation 
considered risks and opportunities associated with these impacts and their influence on financial performance and position across near, medium, and long-term horizons. Senior leadership validated the financial relevance and priority of each topic.
Stakeholder inputs collected 
through structured engagement supported topic prioritisation and placement across the Materiality Matrix. The final list of significant topics is embedded within the ERM framework, reinforcing accountability and action planning across the organisation. The material topics are reviewed annually, and the materiality assessment is being carried out every 3-4 years depending upon the boundary and operations.

Intelligence Powering 
ResilienceRisk Management
We operate in an ever-evolving environment categorised by shifting policies, 
fuel dynamics, technology disruption, climate concerns, and geopolitical events. Embedding risk management into decision-making enables us to protect value, maintain operational excellence, and build long-term resilience.
Our approach integrates risk considerations into 
strategic decision-making, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. This approach aligns with our commitment to sustainable growth, resilience, and delivering affordable, reliable power while navigating regulatory, environmental, and market challenges inherent to coal-based thermal generation in India. In FY 2025-26, we further strengthened our ERM processes to address emerging challenges, including the transition towards cleaner energy and geopolitical uncertainties affecting fuel supply chains.In an increasingly dynamic and regulated energy landscape, effective risk management is pivotal to ensuring the long-term sustainability and operational resilience. As a leading player in the Power sector, we adopt a comprehensive Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework aligned with global best practices and Indian regulatory requirements, such as those outlined by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and the Companies Act, 2013. Risk Management Policy and 
Framework
We have established a structured 
Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework to identify, assess, mitigate, and monitor risks across the organisation. This framework enables us to proactively identify, assess, mitigate, and monitor risks that could impact on our business objectives, financial performance, and stakeholder value. 
Our risk management framework 
is based on ISO 31000:2018 standard & the COSO framework and covers various aspects of the business. The framework is embedded in our decision-making processes and supports strategic growth, operational excellence, and stakeholder value creation. It facilitates the identification and mitigation of risks at enterprise and operational levels, with annual assessments and continuous monitoring of emerging threats. 
Risks are categorised into strategic, 
tactical, and operational types. We maintain a central risk register for the organisation. Risk analysis evaluates uncertainties, sources, consequences, likelihood, scenarios, existing controls, and their effectiveness. Risks are prioritised based on likelihood, impact, and controllability, with clear lead and lag indicators, risk thresholds, and performance metrics.
Risk Governance
Risk governance structure has a three-tier consisting of Board level, Executive level and Operational level. The Oversight begins at the Board level with the Risk Management Committee (RMC), comprising independent directors. The RMC defines the risk appetite and tolerance, oversees the framework, and reviews internal and external risks. It is supported by four sub-committees: Mergers and Acquisitions Risk Committee, Legal/Regulatory and Tax Risk Committee, Reputation Risk Committee, and Commodity Price Risk Committee. The Audit Committee separately monitors financial risks, including interest rate and currency exposures.
At the executive level, the 
Business Risk Management Committee (BRMC), coordinated by the Chief Risk Officer (CRO), drives implementation and reports to the RMC.
At the operational level, Functional 
Risk Committees (FRCs) at corporate functions and the Station Risk Committee (SRC) at plant locations handle specific risk domains and report quarterly to the Chief Risk Officer. SRCs and FRCs identify and mitigate site/function-level risks, with each risk assigned clear ownership. 
This three-tier structure ensures 
risks are managed close to the source while maintaining strategic oversight. The framework is reviewed annually for relevance amid evolving industry dynamics, regulatory changes, and other considerations.
Risk analysis at APL is conducted considering the following dimensions:
Risk Management Process
The risk management process of APL is based on the risk management policy, and the ERM framework. The risk management policy establishes the management intent to effectively manage the risks to the business objectives, the ERM framework establishes the process of implementing the policy. The risk management process of APL consists of five stages:Risk Identification
Risks are identified at enterprise and operational levels through structured assessment of sources of risk, potential risk events and consideration of factors that may influence strategic objectives. These include internal (operations, projects) and external (regulatory, market, geopolitical) factors. All identified risks are documented in a structured risk register, with clear descriptions, ownership, and linkages to objectives. Periodic review is conducted to add new risks and remove obsolete risks.
Risk Analysis
Each identified risk is analysed to develop an understanding about its nature, sources, and potential consequences. This analysis provides an estimate of the level of risk and to form the basis for further steps of risk evaluation and treatment decisions.
Likelihood: The  
probability or  frequency of the risk occurringExisting controls: Current measures in place to prevent, detect, or mitigate the riskControl effectiveness: The adequacy and reliability of existing controlsImpact: The potential consequences if the risk materialises (financial, operational, safety, legal, reputational, or strategic impact)

Risks are prioritised based on impact score, velocity, and controllability, and categorised as strategic, tactical, or operational events. Risk Treatment
We follow the ‘4T’ approach for risk treatment:
 T
olerate - Accept risks where

 T

partners, contracts, or insurance
 T
erminate - Avoid risks that could 
materially hinder operations or outcomes
Post-mitigation residual risks are scored and assigned to dedicated Risk Owners and Risk Champions for implementation and monitoring. Mitigation plans outline actions required, expected benefits, cost implications, monitoring indicators, and completion timelines. Oversight is provided by Functional and Station Risk Committees to ensure timely execution.
Review and Monitoring
Risk mitigation progress is reviewed regularly to track trends and prioritise actions. Station and Functional Risk Committees report to BRMC, which evaluates mitigation effectiveness and highlights areas requiring management focus. We integrate learnings from incidents, stakeholder feedback, and industry benchmarks to strengthen controls.
Risk Culture
We foster a culture of ownership and awareness across all levels. Teams are trained on risk principles, and executives oversee operational vulnerabilities such as fuel cost changes, equipment performance, and safety metrics.
Station leaders actively identify 
and address emerging issues, supported by open communication practices and cross-functional interactions. Performance-linked incentives encourage accountability towards efficiency and environmental priorities.
Recognising climate-related 
risks, we continue to pursue efficiency improvements, cleaner fuel initiatives, and pilots such as green ammonia co-firing to reduce environmental impact while meeting India’s growing demand for reliable baseload power.
Using the structure risk 
management process provides Adani Power with a disciplined and consistent approach to understanding uncertainty and its potential impact on objectives.

Operational Performance

Operational Excellence
Our operating model is 
structured to manage scale and complexity within evolving power sector dynamics. This is anchored in a predominantly Power Purchase Agreements (PPA)-secured generation portfolio, which defines despatch planning and provides clarity of offtake across operating cycles. That structure informs plant-level execution, reflected in sustained availability and consistent Plant Load Factors (PLF) through standardised operating protocols aligned with grid requirements. Integrated fuel sourcing and coordinated logistics support continuity across plants. The Energy Network Operation Centre (ENOC) provides centralised monitoring, real-time performance visibility, and coordination across assets, enabling consistent execution and control across a geographically diversified portfolio.

Mundra
Adani Power Mundra operates as a large, 
single-location thermal power plant with a cumulative capacity of 4,620 MW (4 x 330 MW and 5 x 660 MW). APL-Mundra has commissioned India’s first Supercritical Unit. Mundra Plant reflects early adoption of advanced thermal technology within the portfolio. The project achieved timely execution, including synchronisation of its first unit within 36 months and commissioning of three units in a single year. Spread across 734 acres, the plant is India’s largest private thermal power facility and the world’s first coal-based plant registered with the UNFCCC under the Clean Development Mechanism. A significant portion of the capacity is secured under long-term PPAs, supporting dependable power supply, while the remaining capacity caters to short-term market and energy exchange requirements.

Tiroda
Adani Power Tiroda, located in the Gondia 
district, is Maharashtra’s largest domestic coal-based power plant. The facility operates with an installed capacity of 3,300 MW, comprising five supercritical units of 660 MW each, and serves as a key source of baseload power for the state. A significant portion of the capacity is secured under a long-term Power Purchase Agreement with Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL). The plant incorporates established environmental management systems and is registered under the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) of the UNFCCC.

Kawai
Adani Power Kawai is Rajasthan’s largest 
thermal independent power producer (IPC), with an installed capacity of 1,320 MW comprising two supercritical units of 660 MW each. Commissioned as the state’s first supercritical power plant, Kawai represents the adoption of advanced thermal technology within the regional power mix. The facility is supported by on-site connectivity infrastructure, including a dedicated airstrip, and incorporates established environmental management systems aligned with operational and regulatory requirements.

=== page 62 ===
Unit Startup Tool
Utilising real-time process parameters, 
a machine learning model forecasts subsequent activity sequences and estimates the duration required for each step. Six models have been developed to address WW, HP casing, chest CV, MS temperature, and IP casing temperature. This tool can estimate synchronisation time by analysing the current temperature profile and accounting for the rate of temperature increase.
Integrated Combustion Tool
The Integrated Combustion tool for Unit-1 & 2 recommends combustion setpoints, predicts optimal mill combinations based on coal input, and indicates soot blowing timing and location. Using machine learning models such as principal component analysis, extreme gradient boosting, and Bayesian optimisation, it offers a comprehensive solution to optimise boiler operations and parameters efficiently.
Clinker Detection Tool
The purpose of this project is to determine the tendency for coal slagging and clinker formation by analysing real-time changes in operational parameters using machine learning models. Additionally, it examines how various coal properties influence boiler performance. A comparative classification model was developed to evaluate and recognise patterns from three years of historical data, including both clinker and non-clinker samples. The project focusses on two primary objectives:
 Pr
edicting coal slagging propensity 
based on ash elemental properties
 Det
ecting clinker formation within 
the boiler by monitoring real-time operational parameter variationsCASE
STUDY
Coal Heat Loss Prediction Tool
The primary goal of this project is 
to analyse coal heat loss patterns in relation to the age of coal piles stored in the yard, considering seasonal effects, coal properties, and rainfall data. Using historical data from the past three years, a multi-modal surrogate model was developed to predict coal heat loss and identify the key factors influencing this loss, supported by an explainable AI contribution table
Agentic AI Powered Chatbot
The Agentic Bot leverages a copilot-embedded ecosystem, enabling seamless integration with Microsoft applications for tasks such as querying, document retrieval, and performing actions. This intelligent conversational system can instantly access accurate information from its knowledge base, guide users step-by-step through procedures, and minimise reliance on manual searches. Once added to Teams chat, it is accessible via smartphone as well. Two bots were developed: one answers questions related to the plant technical diary, and the other addresses operational SOPs.

CASE
STUDY
A. VR S afety Training Initiative
 The VR S afety Training Initiative introduced 
immersive, scenario-based learning for high 
risk activities like height work, electrical tasks, confined spaces, and fire safety. With 9 specialised modules and 18 interactive VR videos, the programme enhances practical understanding without exposing trainees to actual hazards. The initiative standardises safety training, improves retention levels, and enables measurable assessment through built-in evaluation tools. Leadership-led demonstrations and early adoption have strengthened the site's commitment to technology-driven safety excellence.
B. Int egrated Combustion Tool
 The Int egrated Combustion Tool analyses 
real-time boiler parameters to provide actionable recommendations for optimised combustion performance. By monitoring key variables such as flue gas temperature, O
2 levels, RH spray, and 
steam temperatures, the system helps operators run boilers more efficiently. This digital tool enhances operational stability, reduces fuel losses, and supports higher boiler efficiency. Overall, it contributes to continuous process improvement and data-driven decision-making.C. Kaizen: Gas A bsorption System
 The Kaizen pr oject revamped the gas absorption 
system used during coal testing in the laboratory, replacing weak plastic-based setups with a robust, reusable metal unit. The improved system significantly reduces exposure to harmful gases like CO
2, SO2, NOx, and CO2, ensuring a safer 
environment for chemists. A new concrete platform for the calorimeter enhances operational stability and minimises heat-related risks. The initiative has improved workplace safety, comfort, and long-term reliability in lab operations.
D. Digital S afety Initiatives (Dashboards 
Implementation)
 APL Raigarh implement ed an integrated suite 
of digital dashboards to enhance safety data visibility and decision-making. The Training Dashboard, Incident Dashboard, Hazard Spotting Dashboard, and ATS Dashboard provide real-time insights into safety performance, incident trends, training compliance, and action closures. These digital tools have reduced manual reporting, increased transparency, and supported predictive risk management. Collectively, they form a comprehensive digital safety ecosystem, transforming the site’s safety governance.

ralised (SOE) sequence of event 
recorder, historian and alarm annunciation systemHooter provision near coal mill: 
A hooter has been installed near the coal mill to provide an audible warning before mill startup. This alert system ensures that personnel working in the vicinity are aware of mill operation and can move to a safe distance. The provision enhances workplace safety, prevents accidental exposure to rotating equipment, and supports safe operational practices in the mill area.
GUI - Fire Water Pump House Parameters:
A user-friendly Graphical User Interface (GUI) has been developed in the control room for real-time 
monitoring of Fire Water Pump House parameters. This interface allows operators to easily track pump status, header pressure and critical alarms. The centralised monitoring enhances visibility of the fire fighting system, supports quicker decision-making, and ensures timely response during emergency situations, thereby improving overall plant safety.
Human Body Static Charge Dissipator 
Installation at 7 Locations:
Human Body Static Charge Dissipators have 
been installed at seven critical locations to ensure safe discharge of electrostatic charges from personnel before entering sensitive areas. Individuals must touch the dissipator handle to ground their static charge, preventing accidental sparks and protecting sensitive electronic equipment. This initiative enhances safety in DCS rooms and hydrogen cylinder handling areas by reducing the risk of electrostatic-related incidents and equipment damage.

Policy Architecture and Management 
Systems
Our environmental management approach 
is anchored in a robust framework of policies that emphasise regulatory compliance, resource efficiency, and continual improvement across operations. It establishes shared accountability for the Board, employees, contractors, suppliers, vendors, business partners, local communities and subsidiaries, ensuring consistent environmental stewardship. Our Environmental Policy Framework 
At Adani Power Limited, sustainability is anchored in strong governance and 
compliance frameworks that enable responsible operations across our value chain.
During the reporting year, we carried out decarbonisation strategy through a 
structured and phased approach aligned with national climate priorities and our long-term net-zero ambition. To further strengthen our preparedness, we undertook comprehensive Climate Change Risk Assessment across operations, covering both physical and transition risks. The outcomes would further support the company’s strategy, reinforcing its commitment to building a resilient and future-ready portfolio. Alongside these priorities, we continued to create shared value for communities around our operations through initiatives in health, education, and sustainable livelihoods, in partnership with the Adani Foundation.
We continue to make measurable progress on environmental performance, 
with emission intensity of 0.86 tCO
2e/MWh, reflecting continued focus on 
operational efficiency and emissions management. Our entity-level specific water consumption stood at 2.13 m³/MWh, well below our internal target of 2.5 m³/MWh. We also achieved 113% ash utilisation, reinforcing our commitment to circular resource use and waste minimisation. Further, we reaffirmed our commitment to biodiversity conservation through endorsement of the IBBI 2.0 Declaration.
In the FY 2025-26, we have also been certified ‘Single-Use Plastic Free’ across 
our operational plants and are working towards achieving ‘Zero Waste to Landfill’ certification across operations, supported by robust waste management systems. All our hinterland plants continue to operate on the ‘Zero Liquid Discharge’ principle, strengthening long-term water security and operational resilience.
During the year, Adani Power was classified under the ‘Leadership’ category by 
CareEdge ESG and in the ‘Aspiring’ category by NSE Sustainability Ratings & Analytics. A score of 69 in the S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA) reinforces our position among leading performers in the sector. These recognitions from leading ESG rating agencies reflect a strong and improving ESG performance, underpinned by robust governance, risk management, and alignment with global sustainability benchmarks.
Going forward, our priorities will remain focused on advancing the circular 
economy, strengthening climate resilience, and embedding ESG considerations more deeply across the value chain.

Performance Monitoring and 
Reporting
At Adani Power, ESG and climate 
governance are seamlessly embedded within leadership oversight and the operational frameworks. Our Board of Directors, supported by the independent director chaired Corporate Responsibility Committee (CRC) provides a robust oversight of our sustainability roadmap, ensuring ESG and climate priorities are weaved into our long-term strategy. The CRC regularly apprises the Board on sustainability performance, risks and progress through its quarterly meetings. We maintain transparency through comprehensive disclosures including SEBI-BRSR filings, ESG and Integrated Reports, investor presentations, stakeholder consultations and engagement forums, CSR impact assessments, social performance reporting and updates on our website. India's aspiration of becoming a USD 30 trillion economy by 2050 requires immense support from the energy sector. India continues to balance the dual goals of meeting rising electricity demand, while advancing sustainability. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the emerging and developing economies will account for 85% of the increase in global electricity demand over the next three years. As one of the fastest-growing major economies, India plays a central role in the global energy transition. Driven by the sustained economic expansion, India’s energy demand is expected to grow at the fastest rate among major economies, with its share in global primary energy consumption projected to double by 2035.
Over the past decade, India’s power 
sector has witnessed strong expansion driven by rising demand, infrastructure development, and strong policy support for both conventional and renewable energy sources. Electricity generation has increased from 1,168 billion units (BUs) in 2015-16 to an estimated 1,709 billion units (BUs) in FY 2025-26, reflecting the scale and pace of growth required to power the nation’s development. Climate Risks and 
Opportunities Assessment 
During FY 2025–26, Adani Power 
undertook a comprehensive Climate Change Risk Assessment to evaluate the potential implications of climate change
on its operations, supporting 
the development of long-term mitigation and adaptation strategy in alignment with global frameworks, including IFRS S2 (Climate-related Disclosures), ensuring robustness and transparency.
The assessment has been 
conducted at plant/location level, incorporating asset-specific exposure to climate hazards, thereby enabling a granular understanding of risks across the company’s operational footprint. Scenario analysis based on IPCC pathways, incorporating Representative Concentration
Internal Carbon PricingPathways (RCPs) and Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) CMIP6 projections has been performed, using Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) to capture a range of
plausible climate futures across 
short, medium and long-term horizons. It covered a detailed evaluation of physical risks, including both acute events such
as floods and cyclones, and 
chronic stressors such as rising temperatures, heatwaves, and water stress. Transition risks have been analysed arising fromevolving regulatory frameworks, technological advancements, market dynamics, legal developments, and reputational considerations. The potential financial implications of both physical and transition risks have been assessed to understand their impact on operations, asset performance and revenue streams.Employee Engagement 
for Energy Efficiency and Climate Mitigation
Our workforce actively participates 
in improving energy efficiency via our internal communication platform, "MAADHYAM". This channel provides an opportunity to them to share innovative ideas with our Chairman regarding organisational strategy, technology, and operations. Ideas that contribute to operational efficiency and climate change mitigation are rewarded with monetary benefits. Additionally, our senior leaders receive performance-based incentives tied to their Key Result Areas (KRAs) focussing on energy efficiency and climate change mitigation.

Climate-Linked Performance Incentives
Climate strategy is reinforced through 
performance-linked accountability across all levels of the organisation. KPIs related to emission reductions, energy efficiency, and climate resilience have been integrated into incentive structures of the leadership and management, including the CEO, the CSO, Environment and Sustainability Manager, and Process and Operation Manager. By linking rewards to climate outcomes, we ensure shared accountability and sustained momentum in delivering our climate commitments.We continuously strengthen the internal capabilities through employee training and awareness programs to embed responsible energy behaviour across the organisation.Adani Power has initiated 
co-firing of biomass pellets at Korba and Tiroda Thermal Power Plants in FY 2025-26. The use of biomass pellets, an eco-friendly, carbon neutral fuel derived from agricultural residues, helps reduce coal consumption, lower lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions, and support circular economy principles. This initiative also aligns with India’s revised mandate of 5% biomass blending from FY 2024-25 and 7% from FY 2025-26, as well as the Government’s SAMARTH mission to promote biomass utilisation. By strengthening local rural supply chains and creating livelihood opportunities for farmers and pellet producers, we continue to embed sustainability and innovation into our operations while advancing national clean energy and air quality goals.Biomass Co-Firing
Alignment with PAT Scheme

The framework serves as a strategic tool to guide investments towards lower emission and cost efficient projects, while embedding climate risk considerations into planning and decision-making. Compliance
Water-related risks are assessed 
through a comprehensive framework to analyse physical risks, regulatory dynamics and stakeholder impacts. The framework addresses dependencies-related risks, including water scarcity, seasonal variability, quality and regulatory challenges. Water-related impacts are addressed through our Integrated Management Systems (IMS) and Environmental Management Plans (EMPs) to strengthen operational resilience.
Managing Water Stress:  
Focus on High-Risk Sites
Our Kawai Thermal Power Plant 
in Rajasthan is located in a water-stressed region classified as ‘over-exploited’ by the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA). Recognising the urgency, we have designated Kawai as a priority site within our water governance framework. During the reporting year, we consumed 2.35 m³ of water in this plant.

Our Biodiversity Lens
At Adani Power, we are 
committed to operating in harmony with nature and minimising our impact on surrounding ecosystems. As we  expand, we remain committed to maintaining the healthy ecosystems around our facilities. 
Biodiversity is a material factor 
for us. We take a precautionary, nature-based approach to minimise ecological disruption, protect natural habitats and responsibly manage biodiversity-related risks across our operational footprint. Our approach is rooted in responsible planning, disciplined execution and continuous monitoring. Governance and Policy 
Integration
Our Biodiversity Policy is embedded 
within the organisation-wide Integrated Management System (IMS) that applies across all subsidiaries, operational locations, suppliers and partners. The policy governs the entire lifecycle of our projects, from planning and construction to operations and restoration, ensuring consistent application of biodiversity standards. 
To embed environmental 
responsibility across the organisation, we deliver regular training and awareness programmes for our employees. Additionally, we have appointed a dedicated ‘Biodiversity Champion’ to lead the implementation and oversight of our biodiversity agenda. Biodiversity considerations are embedded in decision-making across the entire project lifecycle, from site selection and design to operations and closure.
India Business & Biodiversity (IBBI) Signatory
As a proud IBBI signatory, we strategically align our operations with 
IBBI principles to advance the goals of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) through responsible execution, continuous monitoring and active stakeholder engagement.
Read more about our IBBI commitment here
Key Risks Identified
Risk Profile SnapshotBiodiversity Risk Assessment
Adani Power has carried out Biodiversity Risk 
Assessment study and developed site-specific biodiversity conservation plans for implementation. We used a location-specific approach guided by the WWF Biodiversity Risk Filter to evaluate biodiversity impacts and dependencies. The assessment integrates desk-based research, site surveys, stakeholder engagement, and advanced tools such as remote sensing and GIS mapping.

Collaborative Approach for Collective 
Action
We closely work with government 
authorities, NGOs, scientific institutions and local communities to design and implement biodiversity action plans, developed with NABET-accredited agencies using comprehensive ecological studies.
Our Biodiversity Management Plan ensures our operations do not encroach upon ecologically sensitive areas, including protected zones and habitats of endangered species. No species listed on the IUCN Red List or national conservation registers are found within 10-kilometre radius of our operational sites.

Afforestation 
We are committed to comply with the Indian regulatory requirements, including the Forest Conservation Act, 1980, the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA) Act and the Compensatory Fund Act. We intent to avoid forest land wherever feasible and compensate for unavoidable impacts through afforestation and green belt development.
Green belt and green cover across sites are maintained in accordance with the applicable Green Belt Development guidelines issued by the Government of India.
Tree Plantation Pledge on WEF’s 1t.org Forum
As part of the Adani Group’s pledge to plant 100 million trees by 2030, under the World Economic Forum’s Trillion Trees Platform (1t.org), Adani Power has committed to planting 7.85 million trees by 2030.

on working conditions and health and safety 100%Message from the Chief Operating Officer Our Safety Approach
Safety Goal: Zero Health & Safety Related Injuries
Occupational Health and Safety 
(OHS) is integral to our overall ESG strategy. We take a proactive approach to mitigate risks, promote a culture of safety and comply with all the relevant health and safety regulations. Safety expectations are established prior to the onboarding of new employees or contract agencies through mandatory inductions, training, and site-specific awareness programmes. Regular refresher training for permanent and contractual employees reinforces shared accountability.
Policy and Oversight
Our Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Policy guides our safety commitment and measures across the operations. The policy applies to all employees, contractors and individuals under our supervision.Operational excellence remains fundamental to Adani Power Limited’s ability to deliver reliable and affordable power while meeting increasingly stringent performance and sustainability expectations. During the year, APL sustained strong operational outcomes across its portfolio by strengthening asset management systems, leveraging digital tools, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement. We continue to strengthen our operational excellence while steadily expanding our thermal portfolio, with a clear pathway to 42 GW by FY 2032.
Circular economy guided our waste management practices, with 100% ash utilisation achieved through 
productive use in cement, construction, and infrastructure applications. In the reporting year, all our operating plants have been certified ‘Single Use Plastic Free’, and we continue to progress toward ‘Zero Waste to Landfill’ across our operations. In parallel, all hinterland plants operate on ‘Zero Liquid Discharge’ principles.
Occupational health and safety remained a non negotiable priority, with continuous improvement 
driven through leadership engagement, structured training, capacity development and technology enabled incident management. Our continued recognition by national and international safety institutions reflects our commitment to “Zero Harm”. Integrated Management Systems encompassing quality, environment, safety, energy, and compliance provided a unified framework for continual improvement.
Focused initiatives to optimise station heat rate, reduce auxiliary power consumption, and minimise 
forced outages delivered substantial efficiency improvement across power stations. APL has strengthened sourcing strategies through diversified supply arrangements, increased reliance on domestic linkages, captive mine integration, optimisation of coal blending and inventory management, enabling to mitigate market volatility, improve cost effectiveness, and ensure uninterrupted power supply.
We continue to focus on optimising the performance and resilience through data driven operations, 
standardisation, and responsible resource utilisation. This approach is intended to strengthen grid support capabilities while positioning operations to respond effectively to future regulatory, technological, and sustainability expectations, thereby enabling consistent long term value creation.
  Sh. Sudip NagRead about our Occupational 
Health and Safety Policy
Safety Management Systems
We have implemented the Adani 
Group’s Safety Management System framework across all our locations to embed safety, health and wellbeing into everyday operations. The system provides a consistent, and structured approach to identifying risks, strengthening protocols and promoting safe behaviours. 10 out of 13 operating locations are certified 
to ISO 45001:2018 (Occupational Health and Safety Management System). The Safety Management System applies to all permanent, non-permanent employees, contractual workers and all site visitors.
Two-Tier Safety Governance Structure
Our two-tier safety governance operates across corporate and site 
levels, with dedicated committees and personnel holding specific safety responsibilities at each tier. This integrated framework ensures consistent oversight with clear accountability and enables continuous improvement across our entire operational ecosystem.

Technology-led Preventive Safety
As part of our technology-enabled safety commitment, we introduced Thermography monitoring using the 
Fluke camera with mobile and android device, enabling early detection of temperature anomalies in critical and non-critical equipment. This proactive approach supports timely maintenance, reduces unplanned downtime, enhances equipment safety and efficiency, especially for the switchgear.
Safety in Action: Stories That Inspire
Life Saving Response at Adani Power Dahanu
Dr Arjun Sangle’s prompt CPR and responsible actions revived an unconscious individual, turning a critical moment into a life-saved. His decisive actions not only demonstrate his medical expertise and civic sense but also reflect a deeply embedded culture of emergency preparedness and care. Immediate Care on the Road by Adani Power Kawai
Two Sangam Enterprises employees at Kawai plant responded instantly to a roadside accident by assisting the injured and ensuring rapid hospitalisation. This demonstrates our people’s readiness beyond the workplace. 
Safer Roads for All at Adani Power Mahan
Adani Power Mahan installed 112 road signage outside the plant to Parsona road corridor. This initiative enables the safe movement of coal and heavy vehicles, strengthening road safety.

In a rapidly evolving global business landscape with shifting workforce expectations, the Adani Group embeds change management as a core leadership and people capability. This approach enables workforce agility, future-ready skills and organisational resilience to support long-term sustainable growth.

Preparing for The Future
Long-Term Growth Strategy  
at Adani Power
Adani Power’s long-term strategy 
focusses on expanding generation capacity while maintaining operational efficiency and workforce stability. Adani Power aims to scale its generation capacity to ~42 GW by FY 2031-32, while diversifying into nuclear and international projects. This growth trajectory is built on three pillars: Scale, Stability and Productivity. Execution-Led Growth
The organisation is shifting 
from Headcount-led growth to Execution-led growth, ensuring that expansion is supported by stronger systems, advanced technologies and leadership quality.
Strengthening Talent and Operating 
Model
To support this multi
-
year 
pipeline of thermal, nuclear, and 
international projects, Adani Power is strengthening its talent and operating model through:

Digital and AI Enablement
AI/ML based platforms such as 
Drishti, Darpan and Beacon enable faster and more informed decisions across projects, O&M, and fuel management. These systems allow Adani Power to manage a larger asset base without increasing supervisory layers, thereby improving operational efficiency and execution speed.
Productivity and Workforce 
Stability
As generation capacity expands 
2.3x (from 18.15 GW to 41.87 GW), productivity improvements are expected to improve the Man/MW ratio from 0.23 in FY26 to 0.13 in FY 2031-32, demonstrating efficient manpower utilisation.
At the same time, Adani Power 
reduced its merchant exposure from ~10% to ~0.5%, ensuring workforce stability, predictable deployment, reduced stress cycles during market downturns and leadership continuity for a long build cycle.
Our long-term growth strategy combines scale expansion with operational excellence, digital transformation, and disciplined workforce planning to strengthen long-term competitiveness.

Cohesive Group CultureOutcomesHR Governance Model
At the Adani Group, a centralised HR governance framework with decentralised execution ensures consistency in HR policies, standards, and regulatory compliance across the Group. This model reinforces a unified organisational culture and empowers individual businesses with the flexibility at the operating level. 
Organisational Effectiveness 
Adani Power is deliberately redesigning its organisational structure by reducing hierarchical layers and adopting a cluster-based O&M models to enhance speed, accountability, and scalability. This leaner, more agile structure improves operational efficiency and responsiveness, while ensuring our organisational priorities are perfectly aligned with national energy goals.

Adani Power adopts a progressive workforce strategy aligned with capacity expansion, project phasing and asset lifecycles. Workforce planning in Strategic Action Plan is demand-driven and based on cluster-based O&M philosophy, enabling optimised manpower productivity and real-time monitoring through digital dashboards. Future-ready talent pipelines are being strengthened through campus hiring (DET/GET programs), leadership identification under the “Power Up Initiative", and structured succession planning, ensuring the timely availability of technical and managerial capabilities as the organisation scales.

Fair and Inclusive Hiring  
Adani Power’s hiring philosophy is grounded in fairness, 
transparency and equal opportunity, ensuring that merit and competency are the sole drivers of the selection process. The commitment is operationalised through a framework aligned to role requirements, competencies, and organisational values. This approach eliminates any discrimination based on gender, caste, religion, region, age, disability, or socio-economic background. Structured selection processes, diverse sourcing channels, standardised assessments, and multi-level interview panels ensure objectivity and consistency.

Internal Mobility

Before seeking external talent, we systematically assess internal fit through transparent Internal Job Postings, succession pipelines and structured talent reviews.

During significant organisational 
transitions such as expansions, acquisitions, or restructuring, Adani Power adopts a responsible transition approach. This ensures that organisational growth does not come at a cost of community or employee stability. Performance Management 
and Talent Enablement
Performance management 
is tightly aligned to STRAP outcomes rather than generic KPIs, ensuring that individual and functional goals directly contribute to strategic outcomes rather than generic KPIs. 
Strategy-linked KPIs focus on 
value drivers such as capacity scale-up, SHR improvement, fuel cost optimisation, digital benefit realisation, and Man/MW and workforce age profile optimisation.
A clearly-defined HoD-level 
ownership matrix across Projects, O&M, HR, Digital, and ESG ensures defined accountability and eliminates role ambiguity. Performance monitoring is enabled through real-time dashboards, which act as a single source of truth. These are complemented by AI-driven predictive insights to enable proactive, data-backed decision-making.Talent differentiation is driven through performance- and competency-based fast-track progression with focussed retention of critical role holders and top performers.
Performance Management 
Linked Succession Planning
At Adani Power, succession 
planning is a strategic outcome of our data-driven Performance Management System (PMS). PMS provides an objective basis for evaluating employee’s against business-aligned KRAs, KPIs, and behavioural competencies. This structured assessment provides key inputs for succession planning by helping identify high performing individuals with consistent delivery record, leadership potential, and learning agility.
Performance trends tracked 
over multiple appraisal cycles provide insights into performance consistency, growth trajectory, role-readiness, and capability depth. These insights support the classification of talent into succession-readiness categories such as ready now, ready in 1–3 years, and ready in 3–5 years. These insights are reviewed through structured talent discussions and leadership forums to build visibility of internal talent pools for critical roles.
The PMS is further integrated 
with Individual Development Plans (IDPs), ensuring that identified employees for succession roles receive targeted development through job rotations, stretch assignments, mentoring, and focussed capability building interventions. This systematic linkage between performance outcomes and development actions accelerates readiness for higher responsibilities.
Additionally, performance 
data along with potential assessments and talent review outcomes support transparent, merit-based succession decisions. This approach strengthens leadership continuity while reducing lateral hiring.
Performance-linked 
strategy ensures organisational growth is supported by measurable productivity gains, stronger leadership capability and disciplined execution 
Diversity, Equity and Inclusion
In line with the Adani Group’s DEI 
philosophy, we are committed to building a balanced, inclusive and diverse workforce by progressively reducing the average age of employees, and enhancing gender diversity. Respectful workplace practices and proactive grievance redressal reinforce equity and inclusion across sites and projects. DEI is integrated into talent strategy and ESG commitments, rather than being treated as a standalone initiative.

Human Rights and Labour Relations
Upholding Human Rights
At Adani Power Limited (APL), commitment to human rights is more than merely a compliance requirement; it is a core value integrated into our growth and ESG transformation agenda.
Our human rights approach is aligned with globally 
recognised frameworks, including the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and the ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work. This commitment is governed by the Board-approved Group Policy on Human Rights, reviewed periodically. Senior leadership provides oversight of policy implementation, with accountability embedded across businesses.  The Human Rights 
accountability starts at the highest levels, with principles integrated into internal policies, operational processes and supplier expectations, extending across all business units, employees, contract workers, vendors and partners.Explicit provisions are

Human Rights and Risk 
Mitigation
Our Human Rights Due Diligence 
(HRDD) framework puts the policy into practice. Aligned with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, and SEBI’s BRSR requirements, this framework systematically identifies, assesses, mitigates and monitors human rights risks across the Company’s operations and value chain.
Proactive Risk Management
HRDD assessments are conducted at the business and site-level, using defined risk scoring, ownership 
and review mechanisms. Risks are evaluated based on the severity and likelihood of impacts, addressed through mitigation controls embedded into operations and procurement. Residual risks are periodically reviewed to enable continuous improvement.

Respecting Labour Relations
Freedom of Association and 
Collective Bargaining
At APL, we uphold the right 
to freedom of association and collective bargaining as a fundamental principle of workplace dignity and inclusion. In line with the Adani Group’s policy on ‘Freedom of Association’, all employees and workers – whether directly employed or engaged through business partnerships – are entitled to associate freely and pursue collective bargaining without interference or discrimination. While none of our workforce is currently represented by independent trade unions or covered under formal collective bargaining   APL is fully 
prepared to comply with the remaining provisions once the necessary rules (which are expected to be effective from April 1, 2026) are released. Internal systems and SOPs have been pre-aligned for swift adoption, underlining the organisation’s commitment to stringent adherence with all the relevant legislations and rules.
Adoption of New Labour Codes
In compliance with the New Labour 
Codes, as notified by the Government of India on November 21, 2025, we have implemented all the applicable provisions across our HR systems. We have also established cross-functional compliance committees for future-readiness. Digitalisation of registers, wage structures, and contractor-related documentation are other key facets of this strategy. We have initiated awareness programmes to update our employees and contractors with the new codes.

and labour relations approach in BRSR on page 382agreements, we actively promote

participatory work environment.

Message from Head - Techno-Commercial
Approach to Sustainable 
Supply Chain Management
At Adani Power, we are committed 
to building a sustainable and ethical supply chain that aligns with our core values and long-term ESG objectives. Our ability to deliver reliable thermal power depends fundamentally on the integrity, transparency and resilience of our procurement practices. Our approach integrates environmental stewardship, social responsibility and ethical governance throughout every stage of sourcing lifecycle, from initial vendor identification to ongoing supplier development and performance monitoring. 
Building Future-Ready Ecosystems
In an era defined by rapid technological transformation, our focus this year has been on strengthening both our internal and external ecosystems to remain resilient, agile, and future-ready. Recognising that our suppliers are a critical extension of our operations, we initiated structured training and engagement programs aimed at enabling continuous upgradation of their technical and operational capabilities.
A key strategic thrust has been our commitment to understanding 
and adopting Artificial Intelligence (AI) and data-driven solutions. Through awareness programs and collaborative sessions, we are helping our people and partners develop competencies that will define the next phase of industrial growth.
As we look ahead, our goal remains clear: to build a 
technology-enabled ecosystem that creates value, strengthens collaboration, and ensures our readiness to navigate future opportunities and challenges efficiently.Our Supplier Code of Conduct
Our sustainable supply chain approach is guided by a comprehensive Supplier Code of Conduct (SCoC) that applies to all our suppliers globally, including contractors, service providers, vendors, traders, agents, consultants, third-party and other representatives. The code mandates stringent compliance with applicable laws and regulations for responsible business conduct across our supply chain ecosystem.
Our Supplier Code of Conduct is 
aligned with the globally recognised standards including SA 8000 (Social Accountability), ISO 14001 (Environmental Management Systems) and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health and Safety)
At Adani Power, we believe sustainable growth is built on shared responsibility. To embed 
sustainability deeper into our value chain, we prefer partners who align with our ESG values and commitment to operational and environmental excellence. Our procurement, operations, and logistics teams work closely to drive innovative and sustainable solutions that improve efficiency. We also invest in building supplier capabilities and ensure they grow responsibly alongside us.

Strategic Approach to 
Promoting Self-Reliance and Lasting Empowerment
Our CSR strategy is driven by the 
belief that sustainable progress is achieved when communities are empowered to lead their own development. Our community development model integrates strategic partnerships with experienced implementation agencies, in-house programme design and oversight, and alliances with sustainability-focussed organisations. We collaborate with local institutions, government bodies, and NGOs to drive lasting impact and transformation at the grassroots.
All the initiatives are guided 
by well-defined governance frameworks, supported by monitoring and evaluation protocols to ensure effectiveness, transparency, and accountability. Periodic assessments, including baseline studies, need assessments, and impact evaluations, enable data-driven decision-making and continuous improvement. By adopting a need-based and participatory approach, we ensure that programmes are tailored to local contexts and respond meaningfully to community needs and aspirations.Target Communities
The target communities consist 
of populations living in areas around Adani Power Plant, railway line and water supply pipeline. Project areas across 16 sites – Kawai, Tiroda, Godda, Anuppur, Korba, Raipur, Raigarh, Udupi, Mirzapur, Cuttack, Dahanu, Pirpainti, Chapar, Thoothukudi, Butibori and Singrauli across 11 states of India. The primary target groups are school-going children, small and marginal farmers, livestock-dependent households, women, and youth who face persistent challenges such as lack of quality education facility, water scarcity, limited livelihood opportunities, and restricted access to healthcare and basic infrastructure.

About The Adani Foundation-
Seva Since 1996 
We implement our CSR initiatives 
through the Adani Foundation, the social welfare and development arm of the Adani Group, established in 1996. For nearly three decades, the Foundation has served as a catalyst for inclusive and sustainable development, translating the Adani Group’s purpose and philosophy into meaningful, on-ground action across India. It continues to walk alongside communities – listening, learning, and partnering to create pathways for opportunity, resilience, and shared progress. 
The Foundation works across 
geographies with a life-cycle approach and inclusive framework to enable change where it matters the most. Currently, it is operating in 7,247 villages across 22 states, positively impacting 13.3 million lives. Its interventions span critical development areas, including education, health and nutrition, sustainable livelihoods, climate action, and community development, with a strong focus on children, women, youth, and marginalised populations. The strategies of the Foundation are aligned with national priorities and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), ensuring that its initiatives contribute to nation-building and holistic development.

CSR Governance
Oversight of our CSR initiatives 
rests with the Board-level Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Committee, which provides strategic guidance and direction. The Committee formulates the annual CSR plan and submits it to the Board for review and approval. Meeting at least twice each year, the Committee reviews performance across key focus areas to ensure the effective execution of CSR initiatives. 
At the operational level, site-based 
CSR teams work closely with the Adani Foundation to monitor, evaluate, and strengthen project implementation across plant locations. This robust governance framework ensures that our CSR initiatives remain compliant, impactful, transparent, and aligned with the evolving needs of the communities we serve.Community Risk Management
Key community risks in areas of 
operation of Adani Power include degrading quality of education, water scarcity, climate
-
driven 
livelihood vulnerability, low levels of skills among youth, and environmental concerns. These risks are integrated into the Enterprise Risk Assessment Process through regular social risk assessments, stakeholder feedback, and site
-
level risk registers and are 
categorised by severity, likelihood, and their impact on community and business operations for a comprehensive oversight.
Mitigation Approach, Monitoring 
and Review Mechanism
All these risks exacerbate the 
vulnerability of the local population which Adani Enterprise’s initiatives seek to address through targeted 
interventions in Education, Health & Nutrition, Livelihoods, Climate Action, and basic Rural Infrastructure Development. Healthcare and Nutrition challenges are addressed through intervention woven around provisioning doorstep primary healthcare services and nutrition to children under 5 years of age and pregnant and lactating mothers. Livelihood vulnerabilities are mitigated by promoting income diversification, skill development, enterprise support, and promotion of sports. Environmental risks are managed through green belt development, continuous monitoring, and compliance with statutory norms. Water and climate risks are mitigated through rainwater harvesting, augmenting water conservation capacity, and Assessing impact of 
operations on communities
We undertake third-party impact 
assessments of CSR programmes at periodic intervals, typically once every two to three years, to assess the effectiveness and sustainability of our initiatives. For projects of significant scale or strategic importance, such assessments are conducted annually, as recommended by the CSR Committee. The frequency of these assessments is aligned with statutory requirements, internal guidelines, and Board and CSR Committee recommendations, ensuring transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement.We have conducted Impact assessments for the following  initiatives:

Health and Nutrition
In rural and remote areas, 
where distance and limited infrastructure restrict access to essential healthcare, the Adani Foundation is bridging critical gaps by reaching the unreached and strengthening local health systems. Our mobile healthcare units, multi-specialty health camps, and rural clinics are vital in ensuring access to primary care to underserved and elderly people with limited mobility. By focussing on both preventive and curative approaches, the Foundation’s healthcare ecosystem is improving the well-being of India’s most vulnerable populations.
Our SuPoshan initiative is 
instrumental in mitigating malnutrition and anaemia among children, adolescent girls, and women of reproductive age. The project empowers village-level volunteers, SuPoshan Sanginis, who serve as catalysts for behavioural change by monitoring health, providing nutritional counselling, and facilitating life-saving medical treatment.
